title_en: Horizon’s Davolos on True Inflation Beneficiaries
title_zh: Horizon Kinetics 的 James DeBolos 谈真正的通胀受益者
subtitle_zh: 拆解轻资本实物资产与特许权，寻找能穿越周期复利增长的真正通胀受益者。
summary_zh: 本期 Inside Active 由 Bloomberg Intelligence 的 David Cohne 主持，对话 Horizon Kinetics Inflation Beneficiaries ETF（代码 INFL）基金经理 James DeBolos，探讨如何识别真正的通胀受益者（inflation beneficiary）。DeBolos 强调核心是剥离出以名义值计价的现金流（nominally indexed cash flow），不能只看名义增长的收入，还要考察销货成本、销售及管理费用（SG&A）与最关键的资本开支（CapEx）；经验法则是回归实物资产（real assets）——自然资源、房地产、基础设施与某些金融服务，但基金真正要找的是能穿越周期复利增长（compound）的受益者。他尤其看重轻资本（capital light）商业模式，并以特许权使用费（royalties）为例：获得对矿山、土地的收入权益（revenue interest），是数量乘以价格的函数，没有运营费用与资本开支，既有高期权价值（optionality）又在颠覆环境中受保护，与需巨额前期资本和维持性资本开支的矿场、地产开发形成对比。DeBolos 强调若承保（underwrite）得当，底层资产的基础回报率就应达两位数（8% 至 12%），资产价格方向只是额外加成，这正是主动管理区别于依赖方向性敞口的 beta 策略之处。节目还谈到交易所因现金流不规则而被折价买入的机会、ADM 作为价格接受者被卖出的教训，以及价值实现须由股东而非债权人或管理层捕获的陷阱，并把 INFL 定位为传统 60/40 组合的长期分散化工具与实物资产的独特补充。
description: Horizon’s Davolos on True Inflation Beneficiaries

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond soundbites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection. I'm David Cohn. I lead mutual fund and active research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Inflation has become a much more important part of the investment conversation over the past several years. For a long time, investors operated in an environment defined by low inflation, low interest rates, and abundant capital. That backdrop has changed, and it's forced investors to think more carefully about which businesses are best positioned when import costs, asset values, and the cost of capital are all moving differently than they did in the prior decade. So today, I wanted to explore an investment philosophy that focuses on just that, how those businesses are identified and valued, where the market may be mispricing them, and how the opportunity set looks in the current macro environment. Joining me to discuss that is... James DeBolos, Portfolio Manager for the Horizon Kinetics Inflation Beneficiaries, ETF, ticker INFL. James, thanks for joining me.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Inside Active，这是一档聚焦主动管理型基金经理的播客，我们不止步于只言片语和标题，而是更深入地探究他们在选股上的流程、挑战和理念。我是 David Cohn，负责 Bloomberg Intelligence 的共同基金与主动管理研究。过去几年，通胀（inflation）已经成为投资对话中越来越重要的一部分。很长一段时间里，投资者都在一个由低通胀、低利率和资本充裕所定义的环境中运作。如今这个大背景已经改变，它迫使投资者更认真地思考：当进口成本、资产价值和资本成本（cost of capital）的走势都与过去十年不同时，哪些企业处于最有利的位置。所以今天，我想探讨一种正是聚焦于此的投资理念——如何识别和估值这类企业、市场可能在哪些地方对它们定价错误，以及在当前宏观环境下机会集合（opportunity set）看起来如何。今天和我一起讨论这个话题的是……James DeBolos，Horizon Kinetics Inflation Beneficiaries ETF（代码 INFL）的基金经理。James，感谢你的到来。

turns.en: Thanks so much for having me, David.
turns.zh: 非常感谢你邀请我，David。

turns.en: So when you use the term inflationary or inflation beneficiary, what characteristics are you looking for in a business? How is that different from just simply owning companies with exposure to commodities or real assets?
turns.zh: 那么当你用通胀型（inflationary）或通胀受益者（inflation beneficiary）这个词时，你在一家企业身上寻找哪些特征？这和单纯持有那些对大宗商品或实物资产有敞口的公司有什么不同？

turns.en: Yeah, it's a great question. And I think that the whole notion of inflation is so nuanced, but at its core, what you're trying to isolate is a nominally indexed cash flow that's generated by that business. And so a lot of people focus on revenues that can grow on a nominal inflation adjusted basis, but that's only half the equation. You then have to consider the costs of goods sold, the SG & A, and then critically the CapEx. And so typically, the heuristic would be to revert to real assets, which I fully agree with. And so that would be natural resources, that would be real estate, that would be infrastructure, that would be certain types of financial services. And I think that that will do fine in a variety of inflationary environments. But what we try to isolate are true beneficiaries of that environment such that they can compound over time. And so we're much more sensitive to the full revenue, costs, capex, and then how that business can evolve through the cycle or multiple cycles to benefit you as an equity holder.
turns.zh: 对，这是个很好的问题。我觉得通胀这整个概念非常微妙，但从核心来说，你想剥离出来的，是这家企业产生的、以名义值计价的现金流（nominally indexed cash flow）。很多人关注的是那些能在名义通胀调整后基础上增长的收入，但这只是等式的一半。你还得考虑销货成本（costs of goods sold）、销售及管理费用（SG&A），以及最关键的资本开支（CapEx）。所以通常的经验法则（heuristic）是回归实物资产（real assets），这一点我完全同意。比如自然资源、房地产、基础设施，以及某些类型的金融服务。我觉得这些在各种通胀环境中都会表现不错。但我们想剥离出来的，是这种环境中真正的受益者，让它们能够随时间复利增长（compound）。所以我们对完整的收入、成本、资本开支，以及这家企业如何在一个周期或多个周期中演进、从而让你作为股东受益，要敏感得多。

turns.en: Okay. And I understand you kind of focus a bit on capital light business models. What is it about the economics that you believe are attractive in an inflationary environment? Maybe even use a portfolio company if you want to illustrate that.
turns.zh: 好。我了解到你们多少有点聚焦于轻资本（capital light）的商业模式。在通胀环境中，你认为其经济性（economics）中有哪些吸引人之处？如果方便的话，你甚至可以拿一家持仓公司来举例说明。

turns.en: Sure. So I alluded to it in kind of describing how we look at and define an inflation beneficiary, but this concept of being capital light is critical. So yes, you have your real asset and your nominally indexed cash flow, but then you need something where there's controls around the costs as well around CapEx. And it's important for two reasons. One, let's say in the left-hand tail of the distribution, that business is much more resilient in a disruptive environment to preserve your capital. And that's equally, if not more important than the right tail, where these businesses can really compound over multiple cycles because of the nature of the business. And so I think there's a lot of great businesses, but one that we've emphasized in the fund and the firm are royalties. So without going too deep into the weeds, juxtapose a royalty where you are getting a revenue interest in a mine, land, et cetera, that is a function of volume times price, no operating expenses and no capital expenditures. That has very high optionality as volume and price grow, but also you're insulated when in a disruptive environment because you don't participate in OPEX and CAPEX. Compare that to a real estate developer, an apartment complex, or a copper mine, where there's a tremendous amount of capital that is front-loaded to develop that asset. It's probably going to be financed with a healthy amount of debt. And then there's a very robust amount of sustaining capex to either grow, improve, or further develop the asset. And so that's why this concept of capital light is so important when you're looking beyond just, let's say, a cyclical trade and looking at a true diversifier to really compound over many years.
turns.zh: 好的。我在描述我们如何看待和定义通胀受益者时其实已经提到了，但轻资本这个概念至关重要。是的，你有实物资产、有以名义值计价的现金流，但接下来你还需要一种能对成本、也能对资本开支加以控制的东西。它之所以重要有两个原因。第一，可以说在分布的左尾（left-hand tail），这类企业在一个颠覆性环境中的韧性要强得多，能保住你的资本。这一点即使不比右尾更重要，也至少同等重要——在右尾，这些企业因为业务本身的特性，能够真正跨越多个周期实现复利增长。所以我觉得有很多优秀的企业，但我们在基金和公司里一直强调的一类是特许权使用费（royalties）。就不深入细节了，把特许权对比来看：你获得的是对某座矿山、某块土地等的收入权益（revenue interest），它是数量乘以价格的函数，没有运营费用（operating expenses），也没有资本开支（capital expenditures）。随着数量和价格的增长，它有很高的期权价值（optionality），同时在颠覆性环境中你又能受到保护，因为你不参与 OPEX 和 CAPEX。再对比一个房地产开发商、一个公寓综合体或一座铜矿：为了开发这项资产，前期要投入巨额资本，很可能还要用相当多的债务来融资。然后还有非常可观的维持性资本开支（sustaining capex），用来增长、改善或进一步开发这项资产。所以这就是为什么，当你不只看一个周期性的交易（cyclical trade）、而是在寻找一个能真正在多年里复利增长的分散化工具（diversifier）时，轻资本这个概念如此重要。

turns.en: Okay. And, you know, I guess how important is commodity prices, or I should say the direction of commodity prices, to the strategy? You know, can the types of businesses that you own compound in value if commodity prices are relatively stable for an extended period?
turns.zh: 好。那么，我想大宗商品价格，或者说大宗商品价格的方向，对这个策略有多重要？如果大宗商品价格在较长一段时间里相对稳定，你持有的这类企业还能实现价值的复利增长吗？

turns.en: Yeah, I love that question because... If we underwrite properly, the direction of the underlying real asset is only additive to the return. So if we underwrite properly, the base rate of return of the asset itself should be double digits, 8%, 10%, 12% at a minimum. And we tend to try to lean into industries where we do think that there is secular growth and potential for appreciation. But again, if we do our work properly, the base rate of return is not sensitive to the underlying asset price. But if we are correct, it is additive to the returns. And I think that's a really important distinction as an active manager versus a lot of beta strategies, which are leaning much more heavily into that directional exposure.
turns.zh: 对，我特别喜欢这个问题，因为……如果我们的承保（underwrite）做得对，那么底层实物资产的方向只是对收益的额外加成。所以如果我们承保得当，资产本身的基础回报率（base rate of return）就应该是两位数，至少 8%、10%、12%。我们往往会倾向于布局那些我们确实认为存在长期增长（secular growth）和升值潜力的行业。但同样，如果我们把工作做扎实了，基础回报率对底层资产价格并不敏感。而如果我们判断正确，它才会对收益形成加成。我觉得这是作为一名主动管理者，与很多 beta 策略相比一个非常重要的区别——后者要更重地依赖于那种方向性敞口。

turns.en: Okay. And you alluded to this kind of at the very beginning, but I think a lot of investors... have a hard time understanding why the focus on business models. I think a lot of investors just think inflation protection in terms of asset classes, whether that's commodities, tips, gold, infrastructure. Can you kind of go a little deeper into why you focus more on the business models?
turns.zh: 好。你在开头其实提到了这一点，但我觉得很多投资者……很难理解为什么要聚焦于商业模式。我想很多投资者只是从资产类别的角度来思考通胀保护，不管是大宗商品、TIPS（通胀保值债券）、黄金还是基础设施。你能不能再深入讲讲，为什么你更聚焦于商业模式？

turns.en: Sure. Maybe a little history of my experience investing in real assets will frame the discussion well, where I was fortunate enough to join Horizon Kinetics coming directly out of in the run-up to what was the global financial crisis. But I was investing, assigned actually at Horizon, in early iterations of financial exchanges, independent power producers, and royalties in the form of a tax, or excuse me, it was actually an IPO and another was a dormant land trust. And This was very formative in my experience in really understanding the resilience or lack thereof of businesses when you go through something as disruptive as the global financial crisis, where I did an ex post facto analysis in 2013 and 14, and that's where we really came up with this concept of capital life. And a lot of investors and advisors look at a heuristic of asset classes to participate in a certain economic growth rate inflation regime. And I think my experience by kind of in the run-up, the global financial crisis and the recovery illustrated is that you really can't look at any prior cycles as having proper analogs. And one of the biggest distinctions of the current cycle, you really have to zoom out and look at kind of what got us here. So your point, if you look at real estate, if you look at global listed infrastructure, if you look at a lot of these resource-based businesses, prior cycles are probably not that informative because you came into this cycle through an artificially inflated environment where interest rates were so low for so long. The capitalization rates were compressed so tight in anything that had a yield, particularly something that had a growing or nominally indexed yield. Similarly, you had gone through such an enormous build-out in the commodity, what was then called the super cycle in the mid-2000s related to China and India and other emergent economies, mostly in Southeast Asia, that now I think as you look at the commodity complex, you really have to think about, okay, as you get beyond this existing asset base, what's the ability to reinvest that capital effectively? And so the main kind of moral of the story is while it's easy to just kind of look in the rear view mirror to frame your opinion, I think you have to look at every cycle and how asset prices behaved with particular attention to what was the starting valuation? What were the drivers of the asset price? Was it multiple expansion? Was it net operating income growth? Was it kind of going into this kind of secular growth phase? rather than kind of just looking at it in terms of kind of painting by number in an asset allocation mix. And so obviously I think that this is a, there are no analogs for what we're going through today. And I think that every business needs to be reviewed as such kind of looking at how could this business be resilient in a very uncertain kind of forward environment of growth rates and inflation.
turns.zh: 好的。也许讲一点我投资实物资产的经历，能很好地为这次讨论搭个框架。当时我很幸运，在全球金融危机爆发前夕加入了 Horizon Kinetics。我在 Horizon 实际被分配去投资的，是金融交易所、独立发电商（independent power producers）的早期形态，还有以某种税形式存在的特许权——啊不好意思，其实那是一次 IPO，另一个则是一个休眠土地信托（dormant land trust）。这段经历对我非常有塑造意义，让我真正理解了企业在经历像全球金融危机这样颠覆性事件时的韧性，或者说缺乏韧性。我在 2013、2014 年做过一次事后分析（ex post facto analysis），也正是在那时，我们真正提出了轻资本（capital light）这个概念。很多投资者和顾问会用一套资产类别的经验法则，来参与某种经济增长率、通胀环境（regime）。而我觉得，我在危机前夕、金融危机以及复苏阶段的经历说明的是：你真的不能把以往任何周期当作恰当的可比案例（analogs）。当前周期最大的区别之一，是你必须把视角拉远，看看是什么把我们带到了今天。所以你说的那点——如果你看房地产、看全球上市基础设施、看很多这类资源型企业，以往周期可能并没有太大参考价值，因为你是从一个被人为推高的环境走进这个周期的：利率长时间维持在极低水平，任何有收益率的东西、尤其是收益率还在增长或以名义值计价的东西，其资本化率（capitalization rates）都被压缩得极紧。同样，你在大宗商品领域经历过如此庞大的产能扩张，也就是 2000 年代中期那场当时被称为超级周期（super cycle）的行情，与中国、印度以及其他新兴经济体（大多在东南亚）相关，以至于现在我觉得，当你审视大宗商品这个板块时，你真的得想：好，在超出现有资产基础之后，把这些资本有效再投资的能力又如何？所以这个故事的主要寓意是：虽然只从后视镜里去形成观点很容易，但我觉得你必须审视每一个周期、以及资产价格当时的表现，尤其要关注：起始估值是多少？资产价格的驱动因素是什么？是估值倍数扩张（multiple expansion）？是净营业收入（net operating income）增长？还是它正进入某种长期增长阶段？而不是仅仅按图索骥地在资产配置组合里去套用。所以很显然，我认为我们今天正在经历的，没有可比案例。我认为每一家企业都需要据此重新审视——去看这家企业在一个增长率和通胀都极不确定的前瞻环境中，如何能够具备韧性。

turns.en: Okay. Now that makes a lot of sense. And it kind of brings me to the next part is, you know, as you're looking at these companies, You know, I know I love to hear about it and my listeners love to hear about it. Can you kind of take us inside the research process? Once a company enters your universe, what are the factors that really determine whether it ultimately makes it into the portfolio?
turns.zh: 好。这就说得通了。这也把我引向下一个部分：当你在审视这些公司时——我知道我很喜欢听，我的听众也很喜欢听——你能不能带我们走进你们的研究流程（research process）？一旦一家公司进入你们的研究范围（universe），真正决定它最终能否进入投资组合的因素有哪些？

turns.en: One of the great things about Horizon Kinetics and the research universe we have is that it's very proprietary and We're well known as being a dedicated, long-term committed shareholder in a variety of industries, royalties, exchanges, and businesses of that ilk. And so we're very fortunate that there's a lot of deal flow that kind of comes to us and a lot of idea generation that kind of comes across our desk organically just by maintaining this proprietary universe and kind of network of peripheral players and companies. And so One of the biggest benefits is that when you see something that's interesting, typically there's some analogs that you're familiar with in the past that give you a pretty big head start and how to evaluate that business. So two great examples that again, go back to my early career at horizon over 20 years ago. Now I'd say one is in kind of land and the others in exchanges. So. Murray Stahl, the founder of our firm and former chief investment officer who unfortunately passed away earlier this year, he's well known for recognizing the dormant land value of public companies. And now you're seeing much more attention being paid to these scarce assets. But because of his over 30-year history and involvement with a company called Texas Pacific Land Court, which was previously Texas Pacific Land Trust, When a new company was coming public several years ago with a capital light land-based strategy in the Permian Basin called LandBridge, we knew exactly how to evaluate it. We understood the drivers. We understood the growth rates. And it was a very difficult asset for the market to evaluate because at the time, there was really no appreciation and no direct comparables. And so we were able to get up to speed very quickly, worked very closely with the management team, with the private equity sponsor who we are made very close with today and understand the fundamentals of the business and work quite frankly, very pleased when the market priced it as low as it did on its IPO and we're very aggressive there. Another great example, again, going back over 20 years was Horizon was instrumental in the IPO of the New York Stock Exchange, which back then it actually reverse merged into Archipelago Holdings, which was already public. That company is now Intercontinental Exchange, which is amongst the largest derivatives exchanges in the world. But because we had the ability to understand exactly kind of how these exchanges work and how these businesses evolved, we've been at the forefront of a lot of these emerging exchange business models. And so one more recently that's come public has been Miami International Exchange, MyEx. And so we actually were backing that privately and have had our analysts kind of working with them, developing their corporate strategy. And so I guess the takeaway is by having these decades of experience in these highly idiosyncratic unique asset classes, We kind of know what to look for and we're in the flow of information such that it becomes a really great kind of iterative process inside our research committees.
turns.zh: Horizon Kinetics 以及我们所拥有的研究范围，一大好处在于它非常独特专有（proprietary）。众所周知，在很多行业——特许权、交易所以及诸如此类的企业——我们都是一名专注、长期承诺的股东。所以我很幸运，光是靠维护这套专有研究范围和外围参与者、公司的网络，就会有很多交易流（deal flow）主动找上门来，很多投资想法也会自然而然地出现在我们桌上。因此，最大的好处之一是：当你看到一个有意思的标的时，通常过去会有一些你熟悉的、可比案例（analogs），让你在如何评估这家企业上有一个相当大的先发优势。举两个很好的例子，同样可以追溯到我在 Horizon 二十多年前职业生涯早期。我想说一个在土地领域，另一个在交易所领域。Murray Stahl，我们公司的创始人、前首席投资官，很遗憾在今年早些时候去世了，他以善于识别上市公司的休眠土地价值（dormant land value）而闻名。而现在你会看到，人们对这类稀缺资产投入了多得多的关注。但正因为他与一家名为 Texas Pacific Land Court（前身为 Texas Pacific Land Trust）的公司有超过 30 年的历史和深度参与，所以当几年前一家新公司以轻资本的土地策略在 Permian Basin 上市、名为 LandBridge 时，我们完全清楚该如何评估它。我们理解它的驱动因素，理解它的增长率。而这对市场来说是一项非常难以评估的资产，因为当时市场上几乎没有认知，也没有直接的可比对象。所以我们能够非常快地进入状态，与管理团队、与私募股权保荐方（private equity sponsor）紧密合作——如今我们和后者关系非常密切——理解这家企业的基本面。坦白说，当市场在它 IPO 时把价格定得如此之低，我们非常高兴，在那里出手非常积极。另一个很好的例子，同样可以追溯到二十多年前：Horizon 在纽约证券交易所（New York Stock Exchange）的 IPO 中发挥了关键作用，当时它其实是反向合并（reverse merged）进了已经上市的 Archipelago Holdings。这家公司如今是 Intercontinental Exchange（洲际交易所），是全球最大的衍生品交易所之一。但正因为我们有能力准确理解这些交易所如何运作、这些业务如何演进，我们才得以站在很多新兴交易所商业模式的最前沿。所以最近上市的一个例子就是 Miami International Exchange（MyEx）。实际上我们在它私募阶段就提供了支持，还让我们的分析师与他们合作、参与制定其公司战略。所以我想结论就是：凭借在这些高度独特、专有的资产类别里数十年的经验，我们大致知道该找什么，也身处信息流之中，从而让它在我们内部的研究委员会（research committees）里成为一个非常棒的迭代过程。

turns.en: On the flip side of that, though, is there anything that would disqualify a company that might initially seem like a good fit?
turns.zh: 不过反过来看，有没有什么情况会让一家起初看似很合适的公司被淘汰出局？

turns.en: Yeah, we've come across this a lot where we get really excited about a business and it might meet the, all of these attributes. It looks like it's got a great, scarce, unique, real asset. And there's some nuance to the business model and growth trajectory that makes it distinct. And then kind of, we take a step back and we realize, you know, there really is no operating leverage. And these are essentially cyclical beta oriented companies. And, you know, it's, When the cycle is working, a lot of beta capital-intensive businesses, which we will delve into in very unique special situations, might appear to have this nuanced pricing power or non-cyclical growth. Once the cycle maybe flattens out, you realize, well, this isn't as great of a business as I thought. The lack of having any control over either your volume or your pricing or your margins, is typically something that gives us a lot of pause and in some cases will actually sell the investment. In this case, a great example would be Archer Daniels Midland, where we thought early on they were going to be a critical player in the food and ag cycle, particularly going back to the fertilizer shortages. And the thesis around food and ag is just such an interesting thesis with rising global GDP per capita, higher protein consumption, rising middle class, and a lot of these emerging markets. And then, you know, as the momentum settled out, it's like, well, you know, you're basically a price taker and there's a huge new gorilla in the room, which is kind of the Chinese grain and oil processors. So yeah, that's, Again, I think you need to be very careful when evaluating these businesses and really understand where they are in the cycle and is this an anomaly or is this business structurally advantaged?
turns.zh: 对，这种情况我们遇到过很多次：我们对一家企业非常兴奋，它可能符合所有这些特征。看起来它拥有一项很棒的、稀缺、独特的实物资产，而且它的商业模式和增长轨迹有些微妙之处，让它显得与众不同。然后我们退一步，就意识到：其实根本没有运营杠杆（operating leverage），这些本质上就是周期性的、以 beta 为导向的公司。你知道，当周期奏效时，很多以 beta 为主、资本密集的企业——我们会在非常独特的特殊情况（special situations）中深入去碰它们——可能看起来具备这种微妙的定价权（pricing power）或非周期性增长。可一旦周期趋于平缓，你就会意识到：嗯，这门生意并不像我以为的那么好。对自己的数量、定价或利润率缺乏任何掌控，通常会让我们非常犹豫，某些情况下甚至会真的卖掉这项投资。在这方面一个很好的例子就是 Archer Daniels Midland（ADM）。我们早先以为它会是食品和农业周期里的一个关键玩家，尤其要追溯到当时的化肥短缺。围绕食品和农业的这个论点非常有意思：全球人均 GDP 上升、蛋白质消费增加、中产阶级壮大，还有很多新兴市场。然后，随着这股动能平息下来，情况就变成了：嗯，你基本上就是个价格接受者（price taker），而且房间里出现了一头巨大的新 gorilla（不容忽视的新势力），也就是中国的谷物和油脂加工商。所以对，我觉得，同样地，你在评估这类企业时需要非常谨慎，真正搞清楚它们处在周期的什么位置，这究竟是一种反常现象，还是这家企业在结构上就有优势？

turns.en: Yeah. How do you think about valuations for businesses that may have unusually high margins, scarce assets, or strong operating leverage?
turns.zh: 那么，对于那些可能拥有异常高的利润率、稀缺资产或强大运营杠杆的企业，你是怎么看待估值的？

turns.en: Sutter S. Paribas, I would say these higher quality businesses absolutely deserve higher multiples than their capital intense capital head and peers. One thing that I think is challenging for people when they start looking at the higher quality, call it compounders in the real asset ecosystem versus the incumbents that are part of kind of the passive indice mega cap or not mega, but large and more liquid complex is that There is a pretty big valuation disparity, particularly on what's called static yields. So a mine might have a much more robust, call it EBITDA-based yield than a royalty company looking at this fiscal year. But if you're looking at it in terms of an equity shareholder that is building NAV over years or cycles, it's much more important to focus on the terminal value. And that's a unique concept for a lot of people in real assets because they're so focused on these kind of NOI, EBITDA, yield metrics day one. But if it's a depleting asset and you're basically harvesting all this yield and there's no confidence or competitive advantage to then build, maintain, and compound the capital base, then the terminal value is something that's highly subjective and at risk. And so, again, to answer your question, directly, it's a fairly complex discounted cash flow based approach. And we do a lot of work around that, call it 5QX valuation, because by definition, these businesses have much more terminal value than the capital intensive peer groups.
turns.zh: 就你提到的这点而言，我会说，这些更高质量的企业，绝对理应享有比那些资本密集、重资本（capital head）的同行更高的估值倍数。我觉得当人们开始审视实物资产生态系统中那些更高质量、姑且称之为复利型公司（compounders），去对比那些属于被动指数、大市值（或者不算超大市值，但更大型、流动性更好）板块的现有龙头（incumbents）时，有一个难点：两者的估值差距相当大，尤其是在所谓静态收益率（static yields）上。所以一座矿山在本财年可能有强劲得多的、姑且以 EBITDA 计的收益率，而不是一家特许权公司。但如果你是从一个在多年或多个周期里不断积累 NAV（净资产价值）的股权股东的角度来看，那么更重要的是聚焦于终值（terminal value）。这对实物资产领域的很多人来说是个独特的概念，因为他们太关注这些第一天的 NOI、EBITDA、收益率指标了。但如果它是一项不断耗竭的资产（depleting asset），你基本上就是在收割所有这些收益，而又没有信心或竞争优势去建立、维持并让资本基础复利增长，那么终值就是高度主观、且存在风险的。所以，回到你的问题，直接回答：这是一种相当复杂的、基于贴现现金流（discounted cash flow）的方法。我们围绕它做了大量工作，也就是所谓的 DCF 估值，因为从定义上讲，这些企业的终值要比资本密集的同行群体多得多。

turns.en: Okay. Could there be a situation where a company fits your strategy perfectly, but you know, just becomes too expensive to own? Absolutely.
turns.zh: 好。会不会出现这样一种情况：一家公司完美契合你的策略，但就是变得太贵、不值得持有？绝对会。

turns.en: It happens all the time. You know, there's great businesses that we sit back and hope they come down into our buy range. And, you know, a lot of times they never do. Some are actually getting closer today now that you've seen kind of a re-rating in some of the, call it quality compound growth companies. But one of the things that's really instilled in the culture at Horizon is that you need to underwrite with discipline. And we get really excited about businesses and can spend weeks, months, even years on working on them. And then if the math just doesn't work out, then that's just something that you need to live with and hopefully be patient. And if the Fed ever allows there to be a business cycle, maybe you'll get another shot at buying it.
turns.zh: 这种事一直都在发生。你知道，有些很棒的企业，我们就退在一旁，盼着它们的价格能跌进我们的买入区间。而很多时候它们根本不会跌下来。有些如今其实正在接近了，因为你会看到，在那些姑且称之为优质复利增长的公司身上，出现了一轮重估（re-rating）。但 Horizon 文化里真正深入人心的一点是：你需要有纪律地去承保（underwrite with discipline）。我们会对某些企业非常兴奋，可以花上数周、数月甚至数年来研究它们。然后如果这笔账就是算不过来，那就是你必须接受的事情，只希望能保持耐心。而如果美联储（Fed）哪天允许出现一个真正的商业周期，也许你就有另一次买入的机会了。

turns.en: What do you think the market most often misprices the kinds of businesses you're looking for? And does valuation play a role in identifying those opportunities?
turns.zh: 你觉得市场最常对哪类你在寻找的企业定价错误？估值在识别这些机会时又扮演什么角色吗？

turns.en: Yeah, that's actually a great segue from your prior question, because a lot of those companies that we really like but haven't been able to get comfortable with the valuation, it's kind of what I'll call linear versus lumpy. So what I mean by that is the market has always, but particularly in this new volatility beta oriented market, paid a huge premium for the perception of linear stable growth. So there's any number of data companies and payments companies and things kind of in that universe where they've just been able to henceforth grow revenues at a nice, almost double digit growth with steady, if not expanding margins. And because there's a cadence to that where analysts can predict the quarters and the years and have a lot of comfort around kind of the variability or lackadaisical thereof of those cash flows, the market's willing to pay, I mean, until rates went up, just absolutely outrageous. I mean, 40, 50, 60 times for these cash flows. And maybe that would have made sense in a world where your terminal discount rate was one or two, but I don't think we're going back to 0% rates and 2% 10-year treasuries anytime soon. So what we have had a lot of success in is finding businesses that have equal, in some cases, even superior returns. growth, margin, and cash generation attributes to those businesses, but in some cases traded half or less the multiple. So again, a great example would be financial exchanges. So these bourses and exchanges are all over the world and they tend to grow at nominal GDP plus, meaning product development, volatility, velocity of money. They tend to grow in excess, this is revenues, of nominal GDP. with these value or excuse me growth drivers pretty stable if not growing 40 50 60 operating margins because they're basically computers and limited capex because you're basically just updating your computer systems but they have these huge surges in revenue and cash flow when there's a vol of it so you have straight of core moves liberation day and pandemic, like all of these things were massive revenue and cashflow drivers for the exchanges, but then you mean revert to a very nice trend. The market doesn't like that. And so if we're able to buy that at a 30, 40, 50% discount to the smooth inferior cash flows, then, you know, I think that's a great trade. Okay.
turns.zh: 对，这其实是从你上一个问题很自然的过渡，因为很多我们非常喜欢、却一直无法对其估值感到安心的公司，问题就在于我所谓的线性对不规则（linear versus lumpy）。我的意思是，市场一直以来——尤其是在这个新的、以波动率 beta 为导向的市场里——都为那种线性的、稳定增长的表象支付了巨大的溢价。所以有数不清的数据公司、支付公司以及这类领域里的公司，它们就是能够持续地把收入以一个漂亮的、接近两位数的速度增长，同时利润率保持稳定甚至不断扩张。因为这其中有一种节奏，让分析师能够预测季度和年度，并对这些现金流的波动性（或者说其缺乏波动性）感到非常安心，市场就愿意付出——我是说，在利率上升之前——简直离谱的价格。我指的是，为这些现金流付出 40、50、60 倍的价格。也许在一个终值贴现率只有一或二的世界里，那还说得通，但我不认为我们很快会回到 0% 利率和 2% 的 10 年期国债。所以我们做得非常成功的一点，是找到这样一些企业：它们在回报、增长、利润率和现金创造等属性上，与那些公司不相上下，某些情况下甚至更优，但估值倍数却只有一半甚至更低。同样，一个很好的例子就是金融交易所。这些交易所（bourses and exchanges）遍布全球，它们往往以名义 GDP 加上一定的增速成长——也就是产品开发、波动率、货币流通速度（velocity of money）。它们的收入往往超过名义 GDP 的增速，而这些增长驱动因素相当稳定，甚至不断增长的 40、50、60 的营业利润率，因为它们本质上就是电脑，资本开支有限，因为你基本上只是在更新自己的计算机系统。但当出现波动时，它们的收入和现金流会有巨大的激增——所以你会遇到像一些大幅波动、“解放日”（Liberation Day）和疫情这样的事件——所有这些都是交易所巨大的收入和现金流驱动因素，但之后又会回归到一个非常好的趋势。市场不喜欢这种不规则。所以如果我们能以比那些平滑但更逊色的现金流低 30%、40%、50% 的折价买入，那么我觉得，这就是一笔很棒的交易。好。

turns.en: You know, you kind of alluded to this a little bit, you know, in terms of, you know, the edge of your firm is, you know, being to understand, being able to understand these business models. Do you think or I should say, how much of your edge you think comes from identifying the right business model versus just having a different view on whether it's the underlying asset or industry?
turns.zh: 你多少已经提到了这一点，就是你们公司的优势（edge）在于能够理解这些商业模式。你觉得，或者我应该说，你们的优势中有多少来自于识别出正确的商业模式，而不是仅仅对底层资产或行业持有一个不同的看法？

turns.en: I think it's definitely a combination of business model and the correct underlying markets. I'd say somewhere 60-40, 70-30, definitely in favor of the business, the management, and kind of the long-term competitive positioning. But you know, the underlying market absolutely matters. And so you can't really escape that. But I think one of the biggest prerequisites to play this game is to truly have that long-term orientation to preserve your edge. Because again, if we're playing a terminal value that the market doesn't necessarily realize or care about today, The ability to extend your view and look at what this business looks like in five years versus today is really table stakes to play the game that we're playing. And I think the edge is really embedded in that. And then once you have that established, then it's, again, really a function of finding the right assets coupled with the right business model. And then for your earlier question is the valuation. So those are really the three pillars of the process that we have here.
turns.zh: 我觉得这绝对是商业模式与正确的底层市场两者的结合。我会说大概是 60-40、70-30，明显偏向于企业本身、管理层以及长期的竞争定位。但你知道，底层市场绝对重要，所以你没法真正回避它。不过我觉得，要玩这个游戏，最大的前提之一就是真正具备那种长期导向，以保住你的优势。因为同样，如果我们博弈的是一个市场今天未必意识到、也未必在乎的终值，那么把你的视角延展、去看这家企业五年后相比今天会是什么样子，这个能力就是玩我们这个游戏的基本门槛（table stakes）。我觉得优势其实就蕴含在这之中。而一旦你确立了这一点，那么接下来就真的取决于找到正确的资产、配上正确的商业模式。然后就是你早先问到的估值。所以这三者，才是我们这里整个流程的三大支柱。

turns.en: That makes sense. You know, there are a number of different business models that can potentially benefit from inflation or rising nominal activity. And, you know, I know you said your firm is very focused on long term, but, you know, how do you decide what types of businesses are often the most attractive risk reward at any given point in time? I mean, is this something you consider, you know, whether it's portfolio sizing or, you know, just in general? Absolutely.
turns.zh: 这说得通。有很多不同的商业模式都可能从通胀或名义活动的上升中受益。我知道你说过你们公司非常聚焦长期，但在任何一个给定时间点，你是怎么判断哪类企业往往拥有最具吸引力的风险回报（risk reward）的？我是说，无论是组合仓位（portfolio sizing）还是总体而言，这都是你会考虑的东西吗？绝对会。

turns.en: And it really kind of refers back to one of your earlier questions about how important are the underlying asset prices to the return profile. So if we are able to underwrite a base case that we feel very comfortable with in that 8%, 10%, 12% kind of hurdle rate of return, but then also feel pretty comfortable about the downside, And then also maintain what I like to call option value or skew, where there's this really big fat right hand tail distribution around price, around volume, around margin. That's kind of how we like to risk weight and rank the opportunities in our portfolio. And so we're always trying to lock in that really nice base rate of return, but maintain kind of the upside at little or no cost. Something else kind of you mentioned around being dynamic in the market is I think we do have to be aware because the speed at which asset prices move today, we are typically will like to express three, five, seven year views. But if things kind of seem like they're running ahead of themselves or on the other side, kind of getting too far out of favor, we definitely will manage core positions. So we won't fully sell them, but we could add or reduce them based on kind of how we view where they're at in the current market environment.
turns.zh: 这其实又要回到你早先的一个问题：底层资产价格对回报特征到底有多重要。所以如果我们能够承保一个我们感到非常安心的基准情形，也就是那种 8%、10%、12% 的门槛回报率（hurdle rate of return），同时又能对下行风险感到相当安心，然后还能保持我所谓的期权价值（option value）或偏度（skew）——也就是围绕价格、围绕数量、围绕利润率存在一个非常肥厚的右尾分布（right hand tail distribution）。这就是我们喜欢对组合中各个机会进行风险加权和排序的方式。所以我们总是在努力锁定那个非常漂亮的基础回报率，同时以很少甚至零成本保住上行空间。你提到的另一点，关于在市场上保持动态，我觉得我们确实必须保持警觉，因为以今天资产价格变动的速度，我们通常更愿意表达三年、五年、七年的观点。但如果情况看起来像是涨得过了头，或者反过来说，跌得太过失宠，我们绝对会去管理核心仓位（core positions）。所以我们不会把它们全部卖掉，而是会根据我们对它们在当前市场环境中所处位置的判断，去增持或减持。

turns.en: Are you willing to, you know, accept more operating risk if the potential economics are compelling enough?
turns.zh: 如果潜在的经济效益足够诱人，你愿意接受更多的运营风险（operating risk）吗？

turns.en: Absolutely. We call this the opportunistic basket of the portfolio. And so We have our direct asset exposure, our indirect asset exposure, and I'd expect over the fullness of time, those two categories to be 40, 45% a piece. And so that leaves about 10 to 20% of their flex for kind of more opportunistic ideas. And so we are absolutely willing to go into what would be considered capital intensive businesses, but it really needs to fit a couple of important criteria. One is the valuation needs to be very, very compelling, much more so than kind of a quality compounding capital light business. We also want to understand a secular growth dynamic that's not necessarily related to a data or kind of a market, a top-down construct. So if we feel very strong about volumes or price levels or kind of a development schedule, So in other words, they have to be highly idiosyncratic, very asymmetric opportunities. But we've been pretty good at finding these. And fortunately, the volatility and the chaos of the market seems to present them quite a bit today. And so I think it's a really important complementary part of our core capital light portfolio.
turns.zh: 绝对愿意。我们把它称为组合里的机会型篮子（opportunistic basket）。我们有直接资产敞口（direct asset exposure）、间接资产敞口（indirect asset exposure），我预计从长远来看，这两类各占 40%、45%。所以这就留下了大约 10% 到 20% 的灵活空间，用于那些更具机会性的想法。所以我们绝对愿意去涉足那些被视为资本密集的企业，但它真的需要符合几条重要标准。第一，估值必须非常、非常有吸引力，远比一家优质复利的轻资本企业要有吸引力得多。我们还希望理解一种长期增长（secular growth）的动态，它未必与某个数据或某种自上而下（top-down）的市场构建相关。也就是说，如果我们对数量、价格水平或某种开发进度表感到非常笃定。换句话说，它们必须是高度独特（idiosyncratic）、非常不对称（asymmetric）的机会。而我们在发现这类机会上一直做得不错。幸运的是，市场的波动和混乱，如今似乎相当频繁地呈现出这样的机会。所以我觉得，它是我们核心轻资本组合中一个非常重要的补充部分。

turns.en: Also, I wanted to just ask about scarcity and how it fits into your framework of research. Is it Is scarcity of the underlying asset more important or is it the company's ability to monetize that scarcity in your view?
turns.zh: 另外，我想问一下稀缺性（scarcity），以及它如何融入你们的研究框架。在你看来，是底层资产的稀缺性更重要，还是公司将这种稀缺性变现（monetize）的能力更重要？

turns.en: Yeah, that's a really good question because there's actually a lot of great scarce assets in the world and shareholders have not benefited from them whatsoever. And so you definitely need a business model, a management team and a mechanism to where that scarce asset can ultimately benefit your underlying shareholders. You can be patient, but I hate to say you need a catalyst, but there definitely needs to be a bridge and you need to understand the process to crossing that bridge for that value to be realized. And then you know, it's one thing for the value to be realized. It then also has to be realized by you as an equity holder, because you've also seen instances where there's phenomenal scarce assets, but it's in a poor business model or a bad capital structure where more of the value might accrue to the debt holders or management. And so that's a very big pitfall of investing in these types of businesses is you get really excited that you identify a unique, scarce asset, and there's not necessarily a clear way that that gets monetized for your benefit. Okay.
turns.zh: 对，这是个非常好的问题，因为世界上其实有很多很棒的稀缺资产，而股东却丝毫没有从中受益。所以你肯定需要一种商业模式、一个管理团队，以及一套机制，让那项稀缺资产最终能够惠及你底层的股东。你可以有耐心，但我很不想说你需要一个催化剂（catalyst），不过确实需要有一座桥梁，而且你需要理解跨过那座桥、让价值得以实现的过程。然后你知道，价值得以实现是一回事。它还必须由你作为一名股权持有者来实现，因为你也见过这样的例子：有些资产稀缺得惊人，但它处在一个糟糕的商业模式或糟糕的资本结构（capital structure）里，更多的价值可能流向了债权人或管理层。所以这就是投资这类企业的一个很大的陷阱：你因为识别出一项独特、稀缺的资产而非常兴奋，却未必有一条清晰的路径，让它为你的利益变现。好。

turns.en: You know, we talked a lot a bit, you know, about bottom-up investing. You know, I know that, you know, it's a long-term process. You know, do you, or how do you assess the current inflation backdrop without, you know, kind of making the portfolio more of a macro economic forecast? Yeah.
turns.zh: 我们聊了不少自下而上（bottom-up）的投资。我知道这是一个长期的过程。那么你是如何评估当前的通胀背景，同时又不让组合更像是一个宏观经济预测的？嗯。

turns.en: Well, I guess this is very good timing as we're recording here, as we have a new Fed chair and the Secretary of the Treasury has been engaging in some different activities with the yield curve. But inflation is such a personal concept. And so they're doing the best they can by standardizing it in CPI, PCE, and all of these other areas. But I think despite the best of intentions of everybody who might be in charge of the different top-down narratives, the math is the math. And so if you look at the structural deficit that the United States is running right now, the mandatory spending plus interest expense is essentially encompassing 100% of government revenues. And then you have discretionary expenses for things that are pretty important, like defense and NTSB and parks. And so I view the deficit now, we had a chance to fix this, but we missed it. And now the deficit is pretty structural. And so it's easy to opine in your ivory tower that we need to cut spending and balance the budget. I would like that as much as anybody else, but I think it would create a pretty nasty recession. If you look at history, every recession ultimately has much higher deficits than the expansion phase. And so if we're running a 6% or 7% deficit in this type of a leveraged economy, I don't even want to know what the deficit spending would look like if we did allow a traditional recessionary cycle to emerge. So that's kind of the top-down view of just thinking, look, the most beneficial, least harmful, and probably highest politically supported outcome is they're just going to have to try to prioritize nominal growth, which is one part inflation, one part real growth for as long as they possibly can. And People that have looked at different types of trades that they thought were structural guarantees, like shorting the yen for 30 years now comes to mind. These things can last a lot longer than one might think, particularly than where the government now seems to have a lot of tools. So back to your point, how do we, we don't want to make a bet on that by any stretch of the imagination, but we want to have that in the back of our mind around, okay, what assets would do better, worse, what could be exposed, what could be vulnerable and think about, okay, in that world, what types of localized versus broader kind of inflationary, um, sub-industries do we want to be exposed to and so the best in our view are secular growing markets where it's not necessarily as much of a bet on the macro but you kind of look at the underlying fundamentals of these sub-industries and it gets very constructed to kind of underwrite that and then kind of that nominal higher localized inflation is kind of an added benefit to the thesis certainly from a cash flow perspective. And if we're proven right, then obviously I think that there's going to be multiple re-rating on the back end, but that's not part of the thesis. And so again, maybe to paraphrase a longer than intended answer is, we think that there's a very strong, structurally embedded pro-nominal growth backdrop, but it's got to be much more nuanced for you as an investor than just saying, I'm going to own beta real assets because it's going to be there's going to be areas that are deflating, there's going to be areas that are flatlining, there's going to be areas that have huge inflation. And so kind of figuring out where to be in that ecosystem of scarcity, I think is going to be a very important part of investor success.
turns.zh: 嗯，我想我们录制的这个时机非常好，因为我们有一位新的美联储主席，而且财政部长（Secretary of the Treasury）一直在对收益率曲线（yield curve）做一些不同的动作。但通胀是一个非常个人化的概念。所以他们正尽力用 CPI、PCE 以及所有这些其他口径去把它标准化。但我觉得，尽管每一个可能负责不同自上而下叙事的人都怀着最好的意图，账就是账（the math is the math）。所以如果你看美国现在正在运行的结构性赤字，强制性支出（mandatory spending）加上利息支出，基本上已经吞掉了政府收入的 100%。然后你还有那些相当重要的事项的可选支出（discretionary expenses），比如国防、NTSB（国家运输安全委员会）和公园。所以我看待现在的赤字——我们本来有机会解决这个问题，但我们错过了。如今赤字已经相当结构性了。所以坐在你的象牙塔里高谈阔论、说我们需要削减开支、平衡预算，这很容易。我和任何人一样希望如此，但我觉得那会造成一场相当糟糕的衰退。如果你回顾历史，每一次衰退最终的赤字都远高于扩张阶段。所以，如果我们在这种杠杆化的经济体里运行着 6% 或 7% 的赤字，我甚至都不想知道，如果我们真的让一个传统的衰退周期出现，赤字支出会变成什么样。所以这大概就是那种自上而下的视角：看，最有益、危害最小、而且很可能政治上最受支持的结局是，他们将不得不尽可能长时间地优先追求名义增长（nominal growth）——也就是一部分通胀、一部分实际增长。而那些研究过各种自以为有结构性保障的交易的人，比如做空日元做了 30 年这个例子现在就浮现在我脑海。这些事情持续的时间可能比人们以为的要长得多，尤其是在政府如今似乎拥有很多工具的情况下。所以回到你的问题，我们该怎么办——我们绝不想对此下任何赌注，但我们想把它放在脑后的一个角落里：好，哪些资产会表现更好、更差，什么可能会受到冲击，什么可能是脆弱的；然后再想：好，在那个世界里，我们想要对哪些类型的局部性通胀与更广泛通胀的子行业（sub-industries）形成敞口。所以在我们看来，最好的是那些长期增长的市场：它未必是对宏观下那么多注，而是你会去看这些子行业的底层基本面，并非常结构化地去承保它，然后那种名义上更高的、局部的通胀，就成了这个论点的额外好处——至少从现金流的角度看是这样。如果我们被证明是对的，那么显然我觉得后市会出现估值倍数的重估（multiple re-rating），但那并不是论点的一部分。所以，也许把这个比我预想的更长的回答概括一下就是：我们认为，存在一个非常强劲、在结构上已经嵌入的、支持名义增长的背景，但对你作为一名投资者来说，它必须远比简单地说一句“我要持有 beta 实物资产”要微妙得多，因为会有正在通缩的领域、会有持平不动的领域、也会有通胀巨大的领域。所以，搞清楚在这个稀缺性生态系统中该待在哪里，我觉得将是投资者成功的一个非常重要的部分。

turns.en: Yeah, that'll be interesting to watch what happens, at least in the macroeconomic sphere. If we take a step back, if an investor already owns a traditional stock and bond portfolio, how should they think about the role of INFL? Is it primarily an inflation hedge, a strategic equity allocation, a diversifier, or something else?
turns.zh: 是啊，看看接下来会发生什么会很有意思，至少在宏观经济层面是这样。如果我们退一步看，如果一名投资者已经持有一个传统的股债组合，他们应该怎么看待 INFL 的角色？它主要是一个通胀对冲工具（inflation hedge）、一个战略性的股票配置、一个分散化工具，还是别的什么？

turns.en: I like investors that look at it in one of two ways. To your point, I think it's a quality diversifier to your traditional 80-20 or 60-40. But the caveat to that, it's a long-term diversifier. So while we definitely do have lower correlations, and sometimes we can zig when the market's zagging. To really benefit from that, I do think you need to zoom out and take a three, five, seven-year view. Other ways that people look at it is because of the structural constraints of traditional real assets, where again, they're much more captive to cap rates and leverage and capital intensity. It is a very unique complement to traditional real assets. And so I've seen more and more people looking at it as a compliment, not necessarily a replacement to their real estate, their infrastructure, and their commodity portfolios. And so it's a really efficient, unique vehicle that I think if people understand what it's doing and why, it can be utilized in a lot of different ways. But those are my two favorites.
turns.zh: 我喜欢投资者用两种方式之一来看待它。就你提到的那点而言，我觉得它是对你传统 80-20 或 60-40 组合的一个优质分散化工具。但需要注意的前提是，它是一个长期的分散化工具。所以尽管我们确实有更低的 correlations（相关性），有时我们能在市场向左时向右走（zig when the market's zagging）。但要真正从中受益，我确实认为你需要把视角拉远，用三年、五年、七年的眼光来看。人们看待它的另一种方式是：由于传统实物资产存在结构性的约束——同样，它们更受制于资本化率（cap rates）、杠杆和资本密集度——它是对传统实物资产一个非常独特的补充。所以我看到越来越多的人把它看作是对他们的房地产、基础设施和大宗商品组合的一种补充，而未必是替代品。所以它是一个非常高效、独特的工具，我觉得如果人们理解它在做什么、为什么这么做，它可以以很多不同的方式加以运用。但这两种是我最喜欢的。

turns.en: Okay, great. Unfortunately, we need to end here, but this was a lot of fun. James, thank you again for joining me today.
turns.zh: 好，很棒。很遗憾，我们需要在这里结束了，但这非常有趣。James，再次感谢你今天和我一起交流。

turns.en: Thanks so much for having me and I look forward to staying in touch.
turns.zh: 非常感谢你邀请我，我期待保持联系。

turns.en: Great. I also want to thank our listeners. If you liked the episode, please share, subscribe and review. And if you'd like to see more of our research on the terminal, go to BIFundGo for U.S. Fund and active research. Until our next episode, this is David Cohn, Inside Active. you
turns.zh: 很好。我也想感谢我们的听众。如果你喜欢这一集，请分享、订阅并评价。如果你想在终端（terminal）上看到更多我们的研究，请访问 BIFundGo，获取美国基金与主动管理研究。下期节目再见，我是 David Cohn，这里是 Inside Active。
